examples.en: Today is a joyous day for our family.
A baby was born, so the whole house is celebrating.

examples.ko: 동네 사람들이 모여 경사스럽게 잔치를 열었어요.
examples.en: The neighbors gathered and held a festive party.
The news of the acceptance made the whole family joyful.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 결혼하면 정말 경사스러울 거예요.
examples.en: It will be truly a happy occasion if the two get married.

examples.ko: 이렇게 경사스러워서 오늘은 제가 밥을 살게요.
examples.en: It's such a happy occasion that I'll buy dinner today.

explain: '경사'는 결혼, 합격, 출산 같은 좋은 일을 말해서 '경사스럽다'도 집안이나 동네의 큰 기쁨에 써요. 일상에서는 '좋은 일', '기쁜 일'을 더 많이 쓰고 '경사스럽다'는 조금 격식 있게 들려요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라 '경사스러워요'가 돼요.
explain_en: 경사 refers to happy family events such as weddings, passing an exam, or a birth, so 경사스럽다 describes a big joy shared by a family or town. In daily talk people say 좋은 일 or 기쁜 일 more often; 경사스럽다 sounds a bit formal. It is ㅂ-irregular, giving 경사스러워요.

dis.h: auspicious; a joyful occasion or event

p.n: 행복하다 is personal happiness; 경사스럽다 marks a celebratory, auspicious occasion.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 연인에 대한 독점욕이 너무 강해요.
examples.en: He is too possessive of his partner.
The child shows possessiveness over the new toy.
Possessiveness made the friendship difficult.
Love and possessiveness are different.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 독점욕이 강해서 제 무릎을 안 비켜 줘요.
examples.en: My puppy is so possessive that he won't give up my lap.
Excessive possessiveness wears the other person out.

explain: 사람이나 물건을 혼자만 차지하고 싶은 마음이에요. 연인·친구 관계에서 쓰면 '집착', '질투'와 가까운 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. '독점욕이 강하다', '독점욕을 보이다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the wish to keep a person or thing all to yourself. Used about partners or friends, it feels negative, close to obsession or jealousy. Common patterns are '독점욕이 강하다' and '독점욕을 보이다'.

en: be in the way; be a hindrance; get in the way

examples.en: Loud noise gets in the way of studying.
I'm sorry if I was in the way.
I'll go in quietly so I won't disturb anyone.
Please move the things that are in the way.

examples.ko: 이어폰 소리가 옆 사람에게 방해될까 봐 줄였어요.
examples.en: I turned down my earphones in case they bothered the person next to me.
Tell me if it bothers you.

explain: 어떤 일에 걸림돌이 될 때 써요. '방해가 되다'라고도 해요. 정중하게 '방해되지 않을까요?'라고 물을 수 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when something gets in the way of an activity. You can also say '방해가 되다'. A polite way to ask is '방해되지 않을까요?'.

examples.ko: 아침 운동을 하면 힘이 샘솟는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: When I exercise in the morning, I feel energy welling up.
Starting a new job makes my motivation surge.

examples.ko: 아이를 보면 사랑이 샘솟아서 저도 모르게 웃어요.
examples.en: When I see my child, love wells up and I smile without realizing it.
Water started to well up from under the rock.

examples.ko: 좋은 노래를 들으면 아이디어가 샘솟곤 해요.
examples.en: Ideas often pour out when I listen to a good song.
Receiving support made my courage surge.

explain: 샘에서 물이 계속 나오듯이, 힘·용기·의욕·아이디어처럼 마음속에서 계속 생겨날 때 많이 써요. 보통 '힘이 샘솟다'처럼 '이/가'와 함께 써요.
explain_en: Like water keeps flowing from a spring, it is often used for things that keep arising inside you, such as strength, courage, motivation and ideas. It is usually used with '이/가', as in '힘이 샘솟다'.

examples.ko: 이 냄새를 맡으면 어린 시절을 연상해요.
examples.en: This smell makes me think of my childhood.
What do you associate with the color red?
I thought of the sea from that name.
I tried a word-association game.

examples.ko: 여름 하면 수박을 연상하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people think of watermelon when they think of summer.
I linked the two incidents in my mind and became anxious.

explain: '생각하다'는 일부러 하는 것이고, '연상하다'는 어떤 것을 보거나 듣다가 다른 것이 저절로 떠오를 때 써요. 보통 '~에서 ~을/를 연상하다'로 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '떠올리다'가 더 자연스럽고, 어떤 것이 다른 것을 떠오르게 하면 '연상시키다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '생각하다' is thinking on purpose, while 연상하다 is used when seeing or hearing one thing makes another thing come to mind by itself. It is usually said as '~에서 ~을/를 연상하다'. In daily talk '떠올리다' is more natural, and when something makes you think of another thing, you say '연상시키다'.

examples.en: The exam I prepared for so long was canceled, and I feel deflated.

examples.ko: 결과를 확인하고 나니 몸에서 힘이 빠지고 허탈했어요.
examples.en: After checking the result, my strength drained away and I felt empty.
When you feel drained like that, you don't want to do anything, right?

examples.ko: 열심히 모은 돈을 한순간에 잃고 나서 허탈하다고 했어요.
examples.en: After losing the money he saved up in an instant, he said he felt hollow.

examples.ko: 큰 행사가 끝나면 허탈해서 며칠 동안 멍하게 지내요.
examples.en: After a big event ends, I feel let down and spend a few days in a daze.

examples.ko: 그의 허탈한 웃음을 보니 마음이 아팠어요.
examples.en: Seeing his hollow smile made my heart ache.

explain: 기대했던 일이 끝나거나 헛수고가 됐을 때 몸과 마음의 힘이 쭉 빠지는 느낌이에요. '허무하다'는 모든 게 덧없다는 생각에 가깝고, '허탈하다'는 맥이 풀린 상태에 가까워요. 같은 느낌을 '맥이 빠지다'라고도 하고, 명사로는 '허탈감'을 써요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of strength draining from body and mind when something you looked forward to ends or turns out to be wasted effort. '허무하다' is closer to the thought that everything is futile, while '허탈하다' is closer to being left limp and deflated. People also say '맥이 빠지다' for the same feeling, and the noun is '허탈감'.

en: to go crazy; to be mad about; to lose one's mind

examples.en: The traffic is so bad that I am losing my mind.
My younger sibling goes crazy for games.

examples.ko: 시험 전날에 휴대폰이 고장 나서 환장할 뻔했어요.
examples.en: My phone broke the day before the exam, and I nearly lost it.

examples.ko: 그 가수가 나오면 팬들이 환장하며 소리를 질러요.
examples.en: When that singer appears, the fans go wild and scream.
I have a friend who is crazy about spicy food.

examples.ko: 일이 계속 꼬여서 환장하는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: Things kept going wrong, and I thought I would go insane.

explain: 환장하다는 너무 화가 나거나 좋아서 정신이 없을 때 써요. 친구끼리 편하게 쓰는 거친 말이라서 어른이나 공식 자리에서는 쓰지 않아요. '환장할 노릇이다'는 어찌할 바를 모르게 답답하다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
explain_en: 환장하다 says you are so angry or so thrilled that you can't think straight. It is rough, casual speech between friends, so avoid it with elders or in formal situations. 환장할 노릇이다 is a common phrase for a situation that is maddening and leaves you helpless.
